The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the quiet, atmospheric mood of the narrative. The entire "story time" spans only a few minutes—from 6:47 AM to shortly after 6:49 AM—meaning that it aligns very closely with the "real-world time" it takes to read the piece. 

Within this real-time framework, the author uses subtle *compression* to breeze through the routine crossing ("Für ein paar Minuten gab es nur noch das platte, graue Deck...") and effective *stretching* at the emotional climax. When Ilse's phone rings at 6:49 AM, those few seconds of vibration are stretched out to delve into her thoughts, revealing her entire backstory, her relationship with her son, and the central conflict regarding her retirement and the sale of the ferry rights. This deliberate slowing down of time gives emotional weight to her final decision to ignore the call and focus on her work.
